n: After God answers by fire, David declares that this threshing floor will be the site of the Lord’s house and Israel’s altar. The place of mercy becomes the place of the temple.

f.w: This is the house of the LORD God

n: David begins preparing, assigning resident foreigners to cut building stones for the temple.

f.g: Non-Israelite residents living in the land.
Cut and dressed stones ready for building.

n: He stockpiles iron for nails and fittings and more bronze than could be weighed.

f.g: Clamps or fittings to join beams together.

n: Phoenicians from Sidon and Tyre bring great quantities of cedar.

f.g: People of Sidon, a Phoenician city famed for timber and craftsmanship.

n: David reasons that Solomon is young and inexperienced, yet the temple must be magnificent and famous worldwide. So he prepares generously before his death—investing in a work he will never see completed.
David calls Solomon and formally charges him to build the Lord’s house.
David shares his heart with his son: he himself had wanted to build a house for the Lord’s name.
But God told David he could not build it because he had shed much blood in war. The temple, a house of peace, was to be built by a man of peace.
God promised a son who would be “a man of rest,” named Solomon, a name related to shalom, “peace.” Israel would have peace in his days.
Solomon will build God’s house, and God will be his Father and establish his throne forever—repeating the covenant of chapter 17.

f.w: he shall be my son, and I will be his father

n: David blesses Solomon: may the Lord be with you, and may you succeed in building His house.
David prays that God will give Solomon wisdom and understanding to keep His law. God later granted Solomon’s own request for wisdom.

f.w: the LORD give thee wisdom and understanding

n: Success depends on obedience to God’s law. David repeats the words God gave Joshua: be strong and courageous; don’t be afraid or discouraged.

f.w: be strong, and of good courage; dread not, nor be dismayed

n: David lists the vast treasures he gathered “in my trouble”—through hardship and wars. The enormous numbers emphasize lavish dedication to God.

f.g: Through great effort and hardship; or “in my affliction.”

f.w: an hundred thousand talents of gold
f.g: An immense sum, perhaps 3,750 tons; such figures likely stress abundance rather than exact accounting.

n: Skilled workers of every kind are ready—stonecutters, masons, carpenters and craftsmen.
With materials beyond counting, David urges Solomon: “Arise therefore, and be doing.” Preparation must lead to action.
David also commands Israel’s leaders to support Solomon. Building God’s house is a shared work.
David reminds them that God has given them peace and victory. Rest from enemies is the right time to build God’s house.

f.w: hath he not given you rest on every side?

n: The key charge: set your heart and soul to seek the Lord, then build His sanctuary so the ark can have a permanent home. Seeking God comes before building for Him.

f.w: set your heart and your soul to seek the LORD your God

f.g: The sacred utensils of the tabernacle.
